name: Array.from()
desc: Builds a real array from an iterable or array-like value. The optional map function runs during the build, so no second pass is needed.

name: Array.isArray()
desc: Returns true only for real arrays. typeof reports every object as object, so this is the reliable check.

name: array.flat()
desc: Flattens nested arrays up to the given depth. The default depth of one level is often not what people expect from deep data.

name: array.flatMap()
desc: Maps every item and flattens the result one level. Use it when one input item should produce zero, one, or many outputs.

name: array.at()
desc: Reads an item by index and accepts negative values, so the last item is at(-1).

name: array.sort(compare)
desc: Sorts in place. Without a comparator the values are converted to strings, which puts 10 before 2.

name: array.reduce()
desc: Folds the array into one value. The accumulator type can be anything, which is why reduce can build objects too.

name: array.toSorted()
desc: Returns a sorted copy and leaves the source array untouched. The same family includes toReversed and toSpliced.

name: Object.entries()
desc: Turns an object into an array of [key, value] pairs, which lets you use array methods on it.

name: Object.fromEntries()
desc: Builds an object from key and value pairs. It is the inverse of Object.entries and accepts a Map directly.

name: Object.assign()
desc: Copies own enumerable properties into the target and returns it. Later sources overwrite earlier ones.

name: Object.groupBy()
desc: Groups items into an object whose keys come from the callback. It replaces the reduce based grouping pattern.

name: String.padStart()
desc: Pads the string at the front until it reaches the target length. Useful for fixed width ids and report columns.

name: String.replaceAll()
desc: Replaces every match. With a string search it needs no regular expression and no global flag.

name: String.at()
desc: Returns the character at an index and accepts negatives. It avoids the bracket plus length arithmetic.

name: JSON.stringify() with replacer
desc: Serializes a value. The replacer filters or rewrites properties before they are written, which is how secrets are dropped.

name: JSON.parse() with reviver
desc: Parses JSON text. The reviver runs on every key and value pair, so dates and numbers can be restored during the parse.

name: structuredClone()
desc: Makes a deep copy of value. It handles Map, Set, Date, and typed arrays, but not functions or class methods.

name: Promise.allSettled()
desc: Waits for every promise and reports status and value for each one. Promise.all rejects early instead, losing the rest.

name: Promise.any()
desc: Resolves with the first fulfilled promise and ignores rejections. It fails only when every promise rejects.

name: AbortController
desc: Creates a signal that cancels fetch requests and other async work. Call abort to reject the pending operation with AbortError.

name: Intl.NumberFormat
desc: Formats numbers with the grouping, currency, and unit rules of a locale. Reuse the formatter instead of rebuilding it in a loop.

name: Intl.DateTimeFormat
desc: Formats a Date for a locale. Always pass a time zone when the output must be stable across machines.

name: URLSearchParams
desc: Reads and writes query strings with correct encoding. It removes the manual split, decode, and join steps.
